title: Baseten Cuts Qwen3-ASR Batch Transcription Time to Under 5 Seconds Per Hour
summary:
Baseten has improved the processing speed of the Qwen3-ASR 1.7B open-weight model to lower the cost and time required for batch transcription. The new implementation allows for the transcription of an hour of audio in less than five seconds at a cost of $0.0013 per hour, achieving 7x the throughput of stock vLLM on a single GPU.

The company achieved these gains through native audio decoding, KV cache quantization, and a reduction in CPU-GPU synchronizations. Baseten said the 1.7B parameter model currently ranks on the Pareto frontier of the Open ASR Leaderboard as the most accurate transcription model of its size.

Over the last few weeks, I've been optimizing Qwen3-ASR at Baseten. It's now the fastest, lowest-cost way to run batch transcription!

An hour of audio → transcribed in under 5 seconds.
Cost → about a tenth of a cent.
Throughput → 7x stock vLLM, on a single GPU.

The biggest performance gains came from native audio decoding, KV cache quantization, and cutting unnecessary CPU-GPU syncs.
